title: Telemetry Negotiator and Validity Proxy for Incremental Schema Negotiation
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Build a resilient middleware component (Telemetry Negotiator + Validity Proxy) that sits in the usage event ingestion path to perform incremental schema negotiation, soft-enforcement of event contracts, and graceful fallback for unknown or evolving shapes. This ticket implements the service, integrations with the ingest router, and validation telemetry that feeds the Console analytics dashboards. Goal is to reduce ingestion rejections while preserving downstream consumers' schema guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Negotiator service deployed behind ingest-router and exercised by integration tests
Schema negotiation logic supports declarative rules: allow, normalize, annotate, drop, and route-to-deferred-queue
Validity Proxy adds structured failure reasons to rejected events (error_code + hint) and returns 2xx for soft-rejected events so upstream clients use retry/backoff instead of hard failure
Performance SLA: avg added latency < 8ms P50 and < 25ms P99 for the validation step under normal traffic patterns
End-to-end e2e test that validates routing to fallback model and metrics emitted to the Console ingestion dashboard
Feature flag gate for canary rollout and kill-switch that bypasses the negotiator at ingest-router config level
implementation_notes: Architecture: lightweight gRPC service colocated with ingest-router in the same k8s pod group to keep network hops minimal

Schema engine: use the existing schema registry clients but extend to support 'best-effort' normalization rules (e.g., canonicalize timestamp formats, coerce numeric strings) rather than strict rejection
Fallback strategy: route unknown shapes to deferred-queue (Kafka topic) with structured envelope indicating original payload + schema_hint + negotiated_shape_id
Telemetry: emit validation outcome metric (valid|normalized|deferred|dropped) and histogram for negotiation latency. Tag by customer_tier, route, and model_version

Trade-offs considered: strict validation prevents bad downstream materialization but increases rejections. Opting for soft-enforcement to reduce customer-visible errors; will add regressions alerts tied to prompt sets later
Config: JSON-driven rule set stored in ConfigService with hot-reload. Default rules are conservative; PM and Design will update after canary feedback
Compatibility: must be backwards-compatible with existing event consumers (analytics, billing pipelines). Add compatibility shims where necessary
Security: payloads containing PII flagged; forwarding to deferred-queue requires encryption-at-rest and a separate ACL. See Confluence doc link
Testing: unit tests for rule engine, contract tests against billing pipeline consumer, and load test harness (k6) for P50/P99 latency verification
Docs & Runbook: create runbook for on-call to understand common failure modes (rule misconfiguration, backlog in deferred-queue)
